title: The High Monsoon
premise: Freya Okafor, a debt-burdened storm chaser, drags her ragtag crew upriver ahead of the monsoon season, chasing weather data they can sell to pay off the Vane Syndicate. When a flooded riverbank surrenders a salvage chest bearing the seal of Meridia—a nation erased from maps forty years ago—Freya realizes the chest's contents could buy their freedom or bury them. Racing a rival salvage fleet and the rising water, the crew uncovers that the wreck below belongs to Freya's own vanished father, whose disappearance was the price of the Syndicate's rise. In the climax, as the monsoon makes landfall, Freya must choose between the evidence that could restore Meridia's memory and the ransom that would clear her debts, ultimately burning the ransom and keeping the truth. The book ends with the crew, poorer but bound by choice rather than desperation, riding out the storm together in the lighthouse her father once kept.
about_author: Oscar Thornbury is a former merchant marine who spent a decade charting monsoon coasts before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a houseboat, insisting that all good stories begin where the maps run out.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Freya Okafor's POV. A botched storm-data sale leaves Freya owing the Vane Syndicate a sum she can't cover, and their collector gives her until the monsoon makes landfall—six tides. Her crew, a found family of drifters, debates running. The beat is desperation masked as routine, establishing the ticking clock and the crew's fragile loyalty.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Deckhand Milo's POV. While sounding the flooded river for safe passage, the crew dredges up a chest stamped with Meridia's seal—a nation erased from every map. Milo, Meridian-born, recognizes it and hides his reaction. The beat is wonder curdling into dread as Freya realizes the chest marks them for every scavenger on the water.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Smoke on the horizon: the Cormorant fleet, Syndicate-backed salvagers, is working the same river. Freya negotiates a false truce with fleet captain Ilsa Vane while secretly cataloguing the chest's contents—a logbook in her father's handwriting. The beat is the first crack in Freya's certainty: her father's name where it should never be.

chapters.title: Dead Nation, Living Debt
chapters.summary: Navigator Sefa's POV. Sefa deciphers the logbook: the wreck is the Meridian treasury ship, scuttled with proof of the Syndicate's founding crime. Sefa, who lost family in Meridia's erasure, argues for exposing it; Freya argues for selling it quietly. The beat is the family fracturing over what survival is worth.

chapters.title: The Wreck Below
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A night dive in rising water reveals the wreck—and evidence her father went down with it deliberately, hiding the proof inside. Freya surfaces with a sealed letter addressed to her, unopened. The beat is grief ambushing duty; she can't read it yet because the fleet's divers are closing in.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Optimists
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Ilsa Vane offers to clear Freya's debt for the chest's location. Milo, sent to stall, discovers the Syndicate plans to erase the crew once the deal closes—stopping was never an option. The beat is betrayal confirmed, and Milo's quiet decision to lie to Ilsa to buy the crew time.

chapters.title: Three Tides
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. With three tides left, the crew runs the river narrows ahead of the fleet, using Freya's storm-craft to read the water. A near-capsize costs them their fuel stores. The beat is the found family choosing each other over the exit each of them privately planned.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse at Kess
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They shelter at the ruined lighthouse where Freya's father once served. She finally opens his letter: he hid the truth to protect her, and left the choice to her. The fleet anchors offshore. The beat is stillness before the storm—Freya deciding what she owes the dead versus the living.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The monsoon hits as the fleet storms the lighthouse. In the chaos, Freya burns the ransom-value documents and broadcasts the Meridian proof to every coastal station before the storm kills the signal. Ilsa, realizing the Syndicate is finished, lets them go. The beat is the climax: sacrifice of security for truth.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. The storm passes. Debt-free by ruin rather than payment, the crew repairs the boat and chooses to stay together—not because stopping costs less now, but because they want to. Meridia's name is being spoken again on the radio. The beat is quiet resolution: survival paid for, family kept.
